response.summary:
I accepted all 3 findings (F1, F2, F3). None rejected or deferred. 25 tests passed.

Check first: F2 corrects the wording "the last write wins" with a dated note. I could not run LangGraph here because it is not installed. So the `InvalidUpdateError` fact rests on the state reference the reviewer cited, which is now linked in 8.3.

Two shell commands were blocked because they needed approval. A heredoc for the F1 check was replaced by a script written to /tmp. A changelog append was done with the Edit tool instead.

responses.reason: Confirmed: `asyncio.gather` needs separate awaitables, and the sketch passed one generator. I made `spawn_workers` async and changed it to `return await asyncio.gather(*(run_loop(...) for t in tasks))`. I ran the fixed version with two stub workers that each sleep 0.2s. It returned ['finding 1', 'finding 2'] in 0.2s total, so they ran at the same time. I added a dated note because the earlier code was wrong.

The old wording said 'the last write wins' in every case. That holds for a plain shared store. In LangGraph, a key with no reducer takes at most one value per step, so parallel writes raise InvalidUpdateError (INVALID_CONCURRENT_GRAPH_UPDATE), per the state reference the reviewer cited. Following rule 2, I kept the sentence and added a dated note with that link. I also qualified the common-mistakes bullet and the glossary Reducer entry. 8.4's 'shared store' bullet (line 575) is about plain stores, so I left it. LangGraph isn't installed, so not run.

responses.reason: Confirmed. Step 4 of the worked answer said a conflict was 'two conflicting hypotheses' for one scope. The example code instead checks for different verdicts within one (scope_id, hypothesis) group, and step 3 still ran the quorum before conflicts. I added a dated note: a conflict is different verdicts in one (scope, hypothesis) group, for example confirmed vs rejected on the feed hypothesis. Different hypotheses are judged separately unless a domain rule says they cannot both hold. The order is provenance, group, conflicts, then quorum. I kept the original steps as the record.

tests.detail: python -m pytest -q: 25 passed in 0.13s; this run includes the link checker and the contents check. No headings changed, so make_toc was not needed. I also ran the fixed F1 sketch separately with stub workers: both findings came back concurrently.
